title: Ansel and the Autopsy
premise: Elodie Halloran, an estate lawyer with a private habit of solving deaths the police mislabeled, is summoned to probate a will for a man who died two years ago — and whose estate was already settled. The new will names Ansel Voss, a reclusive mortuary assistant, as sole beneficiary and hints that the 'closed' drowning of Elodie's sister-in-law was no accident. As bodies begin appearing dressed in clothes taken from the witnesses' own closets — a killer staging each victim as a memory of the original crime — Elodie and Ansel form an uneasy partnership outside the law. The trail leads to the annual anniversary dinner of the deceased's family, where the final staged body will be raised like a toast. In the climax, Elodie must choose between exposing his late wife's family or letting the truth stay buried; he chooses truth, the killer is unmasked at the dinner table, and Ansel — revealed to be the drowned woman's son given a new name — finally claims both his inheritance and his found family.
about_author: Zephyrine Nystrom is the pen name of a former coroner's office transcriptionist who spent a decade listening to other people's endings before writing her own. She lives in a coastal town much like the one in this book, where she keeps a meticulous file of unsolved local legends she promises are fiction.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. A courier delivers a notarized will dated after its testator's death, naming an unknown beneficiary. Elodie verifies the signature against his own archived files and feels the old itch — the one that has quietly solved three 'accidents.' Emotional beat: dread mixed with exhilaration, the hunter waking.

chapters.title: Ansel
chapters.summary: POV: Ansel. At Merrow & Sons Mortuary, Ansel prepares a body dressed in clothes that don't match the intake report — clothes he recognizes from a photograph on the news. He burns the intake sheet and says nothing. Emotional beat: guilty complicity; we meet him mid-cover-up.

chapters.title: Clothes from My Closet
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Police call Elodie to identify property connected to the new corpse: garments stolen from his own home, down to his late wife's scarf. Detective Ilsa Brandt suspects him. Emotional beat: violation and paranoia — the case has reached inside his life.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Habit
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie, flashback-structured. We learn how Elodie solved three prior deaths through estate paperwork, and why he never told the police. Brandt confronts him with those rumors. Emotional beat: the cost of justice outside the law — isolation.

chapters.title: The Drowned Woman of Harrow Point
chapters.summary: POV: Ansel. Ansel researches the will's testator, Corwin Ashe, and finds the two-year-old drowning of Maren Halloran — Elodie's sister-in-law — ruled accidental. His hands shake at the name. Emotional beat: recognition; Ansel knows more than he admits.

chapters.title: An Uneasy Partnership
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. Elodie tracks the will's witness to the mortuary and catches Ansel destroying records. Instead of calling Brandt, they trade what they know over bad coffee. Emotional beat: wary alliance, two liars agreeing to tell each other partial truths.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. The Ashe family gathers annually to toast Maren's memory; this year's invitation arrives early, with a place card reading ANSEL. Elodie realizes the killer is working toward the dinner date. Emotional beat: ticking clock established.

chapters.title: Second Body, Second Costume
chapters.summary: POV: Ansel. A retired harbor master is found dead wearing Corwin Ashe's missing raincoat. Ansel recognizes the embalming technique — someone trained like him. Emotional beat: horror of kinship; the killer is one of his own kind.

chapters.title: What the Estate Hid
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Digging through Ashe's sealed accounts, Elodie finds monthly payments to a children's home and a birth certificate with a redacted mother: Maren Halloran. Emotional beat: the closed case cracks open — Maren had a child.

chapters.title: Brandt Closes In
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Detective Brandt presents evidence linking Elodie to both staged bodies and offers a deal: confess to obstruction, help her, or be charged. Elodie stalls, protecting Ansel. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth begins to bite.

chapters.title: Ansel's Secret Name
chapters.summary: POV: Ansel. Ansel confesses to Elodie: he is Maren's son, placed for adoption, renamed, and hired by Ashe — who knew — to keep watch over the body until the truth could surface. The will was Ashe's posthumous confession. Emotional beat: raw vulnerability; found family forms.

chapters.title: The Third Staging
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. The family's matriarch, Vivienne Ashe, survives a poisoning attempt but is found dressed in Maren's recovered dress. She whispers a name to Elodie before sedation: 'Tobias.' Emotional beat: escalation — the killer is now killing toward witnesses.

chapters.title: Tobias Merrow
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. The funeral home's heir, Tobias Merrow, was Maren's fiancé before Corwin — and had motive, access, and embalming skills. But Tobias has a verifiable alibi for every staging. Emotional beat: the obvious suspect doesn't fit; doubt spreads.

chapters.title: The Alibi That Was Too Good
chapters.summary: POV: Ansel. Ansel realizes all three alibis trace back to one corroborating witness: Vivienne's caretaker, Ruth Okafor, who logged every movement. Someone fed Ruth a schedule. Emotional beat: the puzzle inverts — follow the schedule-maker, not the suspect.

chapters.title: Maren's Last Night
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie, reconstructed. Witness statements and tide charts show Maren didn't drown at Harrow Point; she died upstream and drifted. Someone moved the body — someone with a boat and a family to protect. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Evidence implicates Elodie's late wife's brother, Daniel, in covering up Maren's death to protect the family name. Brandt pressures Elodie to bury it. He refuses, burning his bridge with the only family he had left. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh; costly choice.

chapters.title: The Missing Beneficiary File
chapters.summary: POV: Ansel. Ansel finds the adoption file Ruth kept hidden for years — and learns Ruth isn't just a caretaker but Maren's childhood friend who has been orchestrating the stagings to force the truth public. Emotional beat: betrayal and pity entwined; the killer is a mourner.

chapters.title: Invitation Accepted
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. Ruth sends a final invitation: the anniversary dinner, one empty chair reserved for 'the truth.' Elodie and Ansel decide to attend openly rather than ambush her, bringing Brandt unofficially. Emotional beat: grim resolve; walking into the trap by choice.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. At the dinner, Ruth rises to toast Maren and reveals the staged fifth body — Daniel, alive but bound, dressed in Corwin's suit. She forces the family to hear how Maren died. Chaos erupts; Tobias pulls a weapon meant for Ansel. Emotional beat: climax — truth spoken aloud at gunpoint.

chapters.title: Raising the Glass
chapters.summary: POV: Ansel. Ansel steps between the gun and Elodie, invoking his mother's name; Ruth disarms Tobias, and Brandt arrests Tobias for Maren's murder and Ruth for the stagings. Daniel confesses the cover-up on record. Emotional beat: catharsis through sacrifice and surrender.

chapters.title: Probate
chapters.summary: POV: Elodie. Weeks later, Elodie executes the will legally: Ansel inherits Ashe's house and the truth of his parentage. Brandt quietly closes the three old 'accidents' Elodie solved, granting them justice without credit. Emotional beat: quiet restoration; law and conscience reconciled imperfectly.

chapters.title: A Family, Found
chapters.summary: POV: Ansel. On the first anniversary dinner since the truth, Ansel sets the table himself — Elodie, Brandt, even a paroled Ruth at the far end. They raise their glasses to Maren, saying her name out loud at last. Emotional beat: resolution — found family, loyalty redeemed by truth.
